text: The images are migrated. This lesson handles the second half of the project -- getting the catalog application itself actually running on vm-catalog01, not just the VM existing.

A VM existing and a VM running the app are two different states. Closing that gap means connecting in, installing the runtime the app needs, copying the application code over, and starting it as a managed service -- the same thing a process manager was already doing on the on-prem server. This is deliberately a lift-and-shift: the only functional change is the image URL update from last lesson.

The default network security group from Lesson 3 only allows SSH. The catalog app serves web traffic, so it needs exactly one more rule -- port 80, or 443 once TLS is in place. Opening exactly what the app needs, and nothing more, is the point. A wider-open NSG isn't a safety margin.

A Running VM status only says the VM is powered on -- it says nothing about whether the app inside it works. Real validation is curl dash I against the public IP, checking for a 200 OK, followed by actually loading the catalog pages in a browser and confirming the product images render from their new Blob Storage URLs.

Consistent with the scope from Lesson 2, this stops here on purpose: one VM, reachable directly, no load balancer, no auto-scaling, no CI/CD pipeline yet. Those are real next steps for a more mature platform -- not what this deadline needs.
With both the images and the app server standing on Azure, next lesson adds the thing the on-prem server never had -- real monitoring.
